title.narrative: Transformation to sustainable crops, livestock and aquaculture food systems in Nigeria

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The project is designed to deliver significant socio-economic benefits, focusing on improving livelihoods, enhancing food security, and fostering inclusive economic development within the target landscape. By promoting sustainable practices across rice, maize, livestock, and aquaculture value chains, the project aims to increase productivity and reduce post-harvest losses, directly improving the incomes of smallholder farmers and other value chain actors. Key socio-economic gains include creating employment opportunities, particularly for women and youth, through initiatives such as integrated rice-fish systems, agroforestry, and value-added processing. These activities will generate "blue jobs" in aquaculture, support women’s entrepreneurial roles in processing and marketing, and enable youth participation in agricultural service provision, enhancing economic resilience within rural communities. The project’s focus on equitable land rights, capacity-building, and financial inclusion will empower marginalized groups, including women and youth, by improving access to resources, credit, and training. By addressing structural barriers such as insecure land tenure and lack of tailored financial products, the project will ensure a more equitable distribution of benefits across diverse stakeholders. Investments in rural infrastructure, such as roads, aggregation centers, and storage facilities, will enhance market access and reduce transaction costs for producers, fostering broader economic growth. Community-based governance structures and multi-stakeholder platforms will strengthen social cohesion and facilitate participatory decision-making, ensuring that the project’s benefits are sustainable and inclusive. Ultimately, the project aims to transform food systems into drivers of socio-economic development while promoting environmental sustainability. As discussed above under Core Indicators, the project aims to directly reach 100,000 smallholder farmers and SMEs—representing about 23% of the target population in the target landscape. Of these 100,000 beneficiaries, an estimated 10,000 individuals would also benefit from enhanced access to finance. Finally, a yet-to-be estimated number of additional indirect beneficiaries will benefit from enhanced ecosystem services, via improved health, nutrition and other socio-economic benefits, including reduced exposure to pesticides, generated by the project. In all cases, at least 50% of the beneficiaries will be women.
